name: Question 13
problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-x{y}^{′}-3y={x}^{4}{e}^{x},\,x>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(x)=\frac{A}{x}+B{x}^{3}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation. 

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result:* 

$$
\int {x}^{4}{e}^{x}\text{d}x=({x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}-24x+24){e}^{x}+C
$$

Question 13
?

Given that the differential equation x2y″−xy′−3y=x4ex,x>0 has the complimentary function yc(x)=Ax+Bx3, find the particular solution yp(x) to this equation.

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result: ∫x4exdx=(x4−4x3+12x2−24x+24)ex+C

a
 yp(x)=(x2+3x−6−6x)ex
b
 yp(x)=(x2−3x+6−6x)ex
c
 yp(x)=(−x34+x2−3x+6−6x)ex
d
 yp(x)=(4x2−3x+6+6x)ex
e
 yp(x)=(4x2−6x+3−6x)ex
Submit
